A REST API plus a published OpenAPI spec (docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml) is the interface other registries implement, so private registries interoperate with existing host support. The registry hosts metadata and delegates security scanning to package registries and downstream aggregators; host applications are explicitly NOT meant to consume it directly but through downstream aggregators (expected pull cadence ~hourly). Private servers are out of scope — self-host a private registry instead. Spam controls: namespace authentication, strict character limits/regex validation, manual takedown; rate limiting and AI spam detection under consideration.
patterns.why: This is the discovery half of cross-native: without a registry the harness can only reach servers a human hand-configured. The reverse-DNS namespace + challenge-based verification is the trust primitive that lets hermes-day show *who* published a server rather than just a URL — directly analogous to the A2A agent-card signature and worth implementing once as a shared 'publisher trust' concept.
patterns.build: `hday_registry.py` (new): a registry client implementing the published OpenAPI surface (search, fetch server.json by name, list versions), with a local cache honouring the ~hourly pull expectation and never fetching on the interactive path. A `Publisher{namespace, verification_method, verified: bool}` normalizer shared with the A2A card verifier so the cockpit's Sources section has one trust vocabulary. Desktop: a 'Discover servers' pane listing registry entries with verified/unverified publisher chips and a one-click install that writes an explicit config entry (never silent). Treat registry metadata as untrusted input: validate against server.json before use, and never auto-execute a command from a registry entry without an approval.
patterns.test: tests/test_registry_client.py — assert an unverified namespace renders as unverified and cannot be one-click installed; that a server.json failing schema validation is rejected with a readable error; that registry reads are served from cache inside the TTL window; and that no registry-supplied command is ever executed without a gate decision record.

patterns.name: Agent-to-agent registries: GCP Agent Registry and AGNTCY Agent Directory / OASF
patterns.what: Two live 2026 agent-registry efforts. GCP Agent Registry: a managed registry for agents, endpoints, MCP servers, tools, bindings, and skills, with a documented data model, automatic vs manual registration, endpoint registration and discovery, MCP-server/tool management, skill registration with revisions, publisher review, search for agents/tools/skills, RBAC, audit logging, and its own Agent Registry MCP server. Its agent identifier is a URN (the OTel agent-spans doc cites `urn:agent:projects-123:projects:123:locations:us-east1:aiplatform:reasoningEngines:456` as a gen_ai.agent.id example) — i.e. the registry identifier IS the telemetry identity. AGNTCY (Linux Foundation): an open collective building Internet-of-Agents infrastructure — Agent Directory Service (a FEDERATED registry for publishing, verifying, and discovering agents and multi-agent applications), OASF (Open Agentic Schema Framework: an extensible, OCSF-inspired record model where agent records are annotated with skills, domains, and modules; a hosted schema server at schema.oasf.outshift.com with validation, decoding, and translation services), SLIM (secure low-latency messaging with pub/sub, streaming, MLS encryption), decentralized Identity (identifiers, verifiable credentials, policy-based access), SHADI (hardened agent runtime), plus observability/eval and CSIT tooling.
patterns.why: These are the registries that make 'cross-provider' concrete rather than aspirational: OASF exists explicitly to describe agent attributes across A2A AND MCP in one schema, and both registries converge on the same idea the OTel conventions already encode — that a registry identifier should be the stable identity used in telemetry. For hermes-day that means the Sources panel can show a remote agent's registry record and its telemetry under one id, and skill registration with revisions gives a real provenance story.
patterns.build: `hday_registry.py`: a second backend alongside the MCP registry implementing (a) GCP Agent Registry lookup for agents/endpoints/skills with RBAC-scoped results, and (b) AGNTCY Agent Directory lookup returning OASF records. Normalize both, plus A2A agent cards and MCP server.json, into one `RemoteEntity{id, kind: agent|server|skill|tool, display_name, publisher, registry_source, verified, capabilities}` type that the Sources panel and `hday_router.py` both consume. Use the registry identifier as gen_ai.agent.id in `hday_telemetry.py` so telemetry and registry entries join. Treat OASF records as untrusted; validate before display.
patterns.test: tests/test_registry_normalize.py — assert an MCP server.json, an A2A agent card, a GCP registry agent, and an OASF record all normalize into RemoteEntity with no field loss for {id, kind, publisher, verified}; that the registry id used in telemetry matches the one shown in the UI; that a record failing validation is dropped with a logged reason rather than partially rendered; and that routing never selects an entity whose verified flag is false when policy requires verification.
